title: Count and name biology items
objective: Use singular, plural and uncountable nouns in a class note.

slides.title: Look at the number word
body: Each takes a singular count noun: each seed. Many takes a plural: many seeds.
Some plural forms change the ending, as in leaf and leaves. Some nouns, such as information, are uncountable.

slides.title: Repair a notebook entry
body: To count information, name the unit: two pieces of information.

slides.title: Read the first case together
body: Lab note with errors: “Each seeds is small. Many leaf are green. We need two information about the plant.”

slides.title: Try it with a partner
body: Each takes a singular count noun.

slides.title: Try a new case
body: Lab note with errors: “Each shells is small. Many branch are long. We need two information about the tree.”

slides.title: Work on your own
body: Repair the last sentence. Keep the number two.

slides.title: Explain a repair
body: Show a partner a number word or each in your corrected note. Explain why the noun takes that form.
